head.citation-title: Comprehensive models and analytical solutions for transient heat transfer in PHC energy pile
head.abstracts: © 2024 Elsevier LtdThis paper presents a comprehensive study of the two-dimensional heat transfer models for four typical cases of precast high-strength concrete (PHC) energy piles. The proposed models adopt the composite section concept and the imaginary source/sink method to solve the heat transfer problem of hollow composite medium with multiple point sources. The effect of multipoint heat sources on the temperature at the calculation point is considered in the multilayer composite medium and a simpler analytical solution than the existing methods is derived. The proposed models are compared with the numerical and in-situ test results of PHC energy piles. The arithmetic examples exhibit the root mean square error ranging from 6% to 36%, which verifies the validity of the proposed model and method. The temperature field achieves a higher uniformity within a range of 2.5 to 3.0 times the pile diameter by using a geometrically uniform pipe configuration. Furthermore, the heat transfer performance of PHC energy piles can be improved by lower convective heat transfer coefficients of the backfill. The study provides a useful reference for the design and analysis of PHC energy piles.

coredata.dc:description: This paper presents a comprehensive study of the two-dimensional heat transfer models for four typical cases of precast high-strength concrete (PHC) energy piles. The proposed models adopt the composite section concept and the imaginary source/sink method to solve the heat transfer problem of hollow composite medium with multiple point sources. The effect of multipoint heat sources on the temperature at the calculation point is considered in the multilayer composite medium and a simpler analytical solution than the existing methods is derived. The proposed models are compared with the numerical and in-situ test results of PHC energy piles. The arithmetic examples exhibit the root mean square error ranging from 6% to 36%, which verifies the validity of the proposed model and method. The temperature field achieves a higher uniformity within a range of 2.5 to 3.0 times the pile diameter by using a geometrically uniform pipe configuration. Furthermore, the heat transfer performance of PHC energy piles can be improved by lower convective heat transfer coefficients of the backfill. The study provides a useful reference for the design and analysis of PHC energy piles.
coredata.dc:title: Comprehensive models and analytical solutions for transient heat transfer in PHC energy pile
